style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: Architectural night photograph, blue hour: a suburban house mid-rebuild after a fire, seen low from the driveway. Charred timber and soot-stained stucco on one side, fresh bare plywood sheathing and a half-stripped asphalt-shingle roofline on the other, poly tarp taut over the gable, one window opening boarded dark. A single warm ochre worklight glows deep inside the open frame — the only warm light against deep charcoal-blue dusk. Slate grey sky, rust-toned burn stains, concrete driveway edge in the foreground. 24mm wide lens, straight verticals, gentle vignette at the frame edges, long-exposure calm, fine film grain, house pushed to the right third with wide empty dusk sky on the left, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks
rationale: The story's stake is not paper but time: a rebuild running after dark while the family lives elsewhere on a capped rent line. architectural_night is the only allowed treatment that can hold that after-hours tension — a dark, unlivable house against deep blue dusk with a single warm worklight — and it matches the vertical's own suggested scene of a house envelope at dusk lit by a workman's site lamp.
cue: the rent money can run out
subject: a fire-damaged house half-rebuilt under scaffolding and tarp, dark inside at blue hour
core_thesis: Loss-of-use coverage pays the rent while the rebuild runs, but it is capped twice — at about 20% of the dwelling limit and on a 12-to-24-month clock — so the rent money can run out before the house is ready.
core_conflict: Two stacked caps — a dollar cap and a calendar cap — squeezing against the real, unpredictable duration and cost of a fire rebuild (contractor shortages, debris removal, permitting, testing).
composition: extreme asymmetry: the half-rebuilt house commands the right third of the frame from a low driveway angle, roofline against a deep dusk sky, generous empty blue negative space upper-left, no people
